summary: WebSocket session handoff causes missing terminal JSON metadata and truncated final tokens
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after a WebSocket reconnect where the load balancer performs a session handoff, the final 'choice' event arrives but its JSON metadata (final tokens, finish_reason) is missing or truncated. Impact: downstream client cannot determine completion and sometimes drops the last 1-3 tokens of the final choice, leading to incomplete sentences in production UI. Environment: Dedicated customer deployment in us-east, traffic routed through streaming-proxy with sticky-session timeouts set to 20s. Occurs intermittently during LB failover and when client reconnects within 5s of disconnect.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long streaming generation via WebSocket against the customer's dedicated endpoint (model=redwood-open-v1-moderate).
2) While streaming, simulate LB probe/failover causing a socket handoff (terminate upstream connection and establish new connection using same session token).
3) Observe stream reattachment sequence from client (client issues resume with existing session ID).
4) Check final choice frame: verify JSON metadata fields (finish_reason, tokens, index) and last text chunks for completeness.
5) Repeat under high concurrency (10+ concurrent streams) to increase chance of occurrence.

comments: Support (Leah Carter) 2026-03-10: Customer reported intermittent truncated final token and empty metadata on final 'choice' event after reconnect. Provided initial logs and short repro steps. Assigning to infra team.

SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Noticed session handoff path in proxy logs; creating local repro harness to simulate LB handover and client quick-reconnect. Marking as P1 due to user-facing truncation.

Customer (Anna Kim, MuseFlow) 2026-03-10: Impact is visible in our editor where last word is cut ~10% of the time when users lose connectivity briefly. We can provide packet captures and client timestamps on request.

SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally when proxy sends final framing across connection boundary during in-flight tail flush. Hypothesis: final metadata is emitted on old upstream connection and not stitched into the resumed stream if handoff occurs before ACK of terminal frame.

Support (Leah Carter) 2026-03-12: Communicated interim workaround to customer: increase sticky-session timeout to 60s and set client reconnect backoff to 1.5s to reduce handoffs. Customer deploying change now.
Engineering (Tomás Li) 2026-03-12: Adding work item to ensure terminal frames are buffered and re-sent on resume, and to add an explicit terminal-event ACK from client. PR in progress.
investigation_notes: Initial root-cause hypothesis: race between proxy handoff and runtime tail-flush. When the runtime emits the final choice + metadata, the proxy sometimes forwards the text frames but drops or fails to attach the JSON metadata because metadata is buffered in a separate control stream that was tied to the old connection. Observed behavior: final text arrives but meta={} or missing. Reproducible when handoff occurs within 200-800ms of final frame emission. Also observed higher frequency under high concurrency and when gzip compression is enabled at proxy which changes chunk boundaries.
resolution_notes: Workarounds: 1) Customer increased sticky-session timeout and adjusted client reconnect strategy to reduce handoffs (applied 2026-03-12). 2) Short-term patch: proxy will now persist and forward terminal-control frames during connection handoff (deployed to staging). Long-term fix: engineering to add atomic terminal-frame emission with metadata coalescing in the serving runtime and an explicit terminal ACK from client to guard against lost metadata. Target ETA for staged rollback to prod: 2026-03-19. Follow-up tasks: add e2e test for session handoff, update runbook, and add dashboard metric counting resume-with-missing-meta events.
